question: network-supply-connection-hv-metering
unit: sum (one complete 300 kVA HV-supplied supply point, live and registered; $/kVA over 300 kVA stated in the basis)

band.unit: sum (one complete 300 kVA HV-supplied supply point, live and registered; $/kVA over 300 kVA stated in the basis)
band.basis: Auckland urban, GST exclusive, Vector network, existing 11 kV in the berm, one Vector-owned 300 kVA ground-mount transformer in a customer-provided substation site, 30 m HV + 25 m LV cable, Category 4 CT metering, one energisation. Sum of the eight components above. Equivalent to $727/kVA (low), $972/kVA (high) and $849/kVA (centre) over the 300 kVA nominal connected capacity. The dominant component (Vector capital contribution, 68-73% of the band) is priced from a published EA P50 proxy for equivalent works, not from a Vector quote: Vector prices this tier per job through a Customer Works Agreement, so treat the band as a cost-plan allowance and replace component 4 the moment Vector issues its CWA. Allowances (Vector assessment/ICP, metering, coordination) total $15,800-$35,000, i.e. 7-12% of the band, so they do not carry the estimate. Reviewer can reject any one component: if the EA proxy already covers the connection cable, strip component 5.

band.unit: sum (one complete 300 kVA HV supply point, live and registered, Auckland)
band.basis: Sum of the eight components above (AKL, GST exclusive, no preliminaries, margin, design/consent fees or site works). Stated as $/kVA over the 300 kVA nominal capacity: LOW $666/kVA, HIGH $848/kVA, midpoint about $757/kVA (arithmetic centre $227,065, i.e. $756.9/kVA). Confidence is LOW because the largest line - Vector's capital contribution for the network-owned 300 kVA transformer and 11 kV protection/switchgear, about 80% of the total - is a proxy: Vector prices the distribution-substation tier per job and publishes no figure, so we have used the Electricity Authority's published distribution-transformer-tier worked example for a new 300 kVA transformer plus RMU, taken at the metro/urban-to-rural spread. All other lines are cited QV rows, cited Vector fees, or clearly labelled allowances, and the allowances are only 4-8% of the total, so the band is not allowance-driven. A reviewer can reject line 4 alone and replace it with Vector's Customer Works Agreement price without disturbing the rest; substituting Vector's own posted DS capacity rate ($176.67/diversified kVA = $53,001) for the proxy would take roughly $105k-$129k out of the band.

band.unit: sum (lump sum, one complete supply point, GST excl.)
band.basis: Add of cited components: Vector design fee $3,000 + Vector site visit $170 + Vector connection works/capital contribution $159,510-$182,010 (EA published DS-tier example at 300 kVA, $531.7-$606.7/kVA) + HV cable $3,750 (QV proxy 125/m x 30m) + HV uplift/terminations/trench allowance $6,000-$14,000 + LV service $20,250-$30,000 (QV 810-1,200/m x 25m) + Cat 4 metering allowance $6,000-$16,000 + coordination/certification allowance $3,000-$8,000. Equals 672-856 $/kVA over the 300 kVA nominal capacity (midpoint 764 $/kVA). Allowances are ~5% (low) to ~15% (high) of the band, so no allowance carries a main driver. Confidence low because the largest component is an indicative EA published example used as a proxy for a Vector charge that is priced per job and not published; the HV cable rate is an LV-class QV proxy; and the EA example overlaps the separately priced cable runs. Reviewer can reject any single part without disturbing the others.

band.unit: sum - one complete 300 kVA HV supply point, live and registered (NZD, GST exclusive, Auckland); also stated as $/kVA over the 300 kVA nominal capacity
band.basis: Sum of the ten distinct components above, no component counted twice. Published Vector figures: $3,000 design fee, $170 first-energisation site visit, and the network capacity cost computed as Vector's own method and rate (300 kVA x $176.67 per diversified kVA for the Distribution substation tier). Vector's dedicated connection assets (Vector-owned 300 kVA ground-mount transformer + HV RMU/protection, installed) are proxied from the Electricity Authority's published Distribution-transformer-tier example ($179.6k metro / $182k urban for a 300 kVA increment including a new distribution transformer and RMU). HV and LV cable come from QV CostBuilder rows (QV has no MV cable, no substation or metering rows). Remaining items are labelled allowances totalling $16,500-$36,500, i.e. about 6-11% of the band, well under one third. GST-exclusive, Auckland urban, normal working hours. Amortisation: low $912/kVA, centre $1,010/kVA, high $1,108/kVA over 300 kVA. KEY BASIS LIMITATIONS, hence low confidence: (1) Vector prices both the connection charge for the dedicated works and the development contribution for a distribution-substation supply 'per job' via a Customer Works Agreement, so no quoted figure exists yet - the largest line is an indicative regulator-published estimate, not Vector's price, and the scenario's own transformer is a single 300 kVA unit so no size/diversity scaling has been applied; (2) if Vector also applies its published HV-feeder-tier capacity rate ($715.89 per diversified kVA) the sum would rise by up to about $215,000, which is excluded on the stated basis that no network reinforcement is required and 11kV already exists at the frontage; (3) metering, HV terminations and coordination are allowances that must be replaced with MEP and contractor quotes.
